Subject: Acme POC — recap and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: move 10k monthly customer support conversations to a Redwood-powered assist pipeline (reduce time-to-response and improve first-contact resolution).
- Success criteria suggested: 80% intent accuracy on top-1 prediction, 15% reduction in average handle time, and no regression in key safety checks.

Proposed POC scope & timeline:
- Week 0: kickoff, data collection checklist + SSO & network tests
- Week 1: baseline eval (offline) on a 1k sample provided by Acme + model tuning
- Week 2: online shadow (parallel traffic) for 3 business days
- Week 3: wrap, handoff docs, and go/no-go meeting

Ownership:
- Redwood: runtime, model selection, evaluation harness, and shadow infra
- Acme: provide labeled sample (1k), success metric owners, and access for shadowing (read-only)

Attachments: I attached a one-page eval plan and an initial rubric draft. Please review and confirm the success criteria and timeline. If those look good, Nathan from our infra team will send the preflight checklist for shadowing.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Alex: confirm success criteria and supply the 1k sample by Thu 6/25
2) Marissa/Rachel: finalize eval rubric and schedule kickoff (proposed Mon 6/29)
3) David: prepare shadow infra preflight checklist and share any network constraints

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.
—

Hi all — thanks for confirming. Attaching a short note on recommended methodology and a first-pass rubric (attached as redwood-eval-rubric-v1.md). High-level recommendations below: 

1) Start with an offline evaluation (1k labeled sample):
  - Purpose: quick, reproducible metric baseline (intent accuracy, false positive rate, etc.)
  - Metrics to compute: top-1 accuracy, top-3 accuracy, false positive rate for escalation triggers, per-intent precision/recall
  - Acceptance thresholds: top-1 >= 80%, escalation FPR < 2%

2) Run an online shadow for qualitative and production-sim checks:
  - Purpose: capture distributional shift, latency under real traffic, monitor safety hooks and reviewer-assisted scoring
  - Duration: start with 3 business days; extend if we identify high variance or high false positives
  - Monitoring: collect sampling of 200 shadow responses for manual review (Priya to coordinate reviewers)

3) Grading rubric (high level):
  - Quantitative (automated): intent accuracy (40%), escalation FPR (20%), latency SLOs (10%)
  - Qualitative (manual review): escalation appropriateness (20%), response naturalness/clarity (10%)
  - Combined pass threshold: weighted score >= 75%

4) Ownership & deliverables:
  - Redwood (Rachel): offline eval harness + automated report, shadow infra setup, and sampling script
  - Acme (Priya/Alex): provide labeled sample, coordinate manual reviewers for shadow sampling

I'll update the rubric file with the weighting and example scoring guidelines. Marissa — happy to take point on the offline run as soon as we get the 1k.

Regards,
Rachel
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
